definition: The practice of including a shared portion of text between consecutive chunks when splitting a document, to avoid losing context at chunk boundaries.
details: Chunk overlap helps prevent important information that spans a chunk boundary from being fragmented in a way that hurts retrieval or comprehension.

explainer.lead: Overlap is the shared portion of text kept between consecutive chunks when splitting a document. It matters because information spanning a boundary can otherwise be fragmented and lost to retrieval or comprehension.

tiers.eli5: It is like repeating the last sentence of a page at the top of the next, so nothing falls through the gap.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers set an overlap window when chunking documents for retrieval systems to preserve cross-boundary context. A pitfall is overdoing it, which duplicates content and inflates index size.
tiers.paperLevel: Overlap is the practice of including a shared portion of text between consecutive chunks to avoid losing context at chunk boundaries; no standard overlap size is specified.

explainer.example: A document split into 500-token chunks with 50-token overlap repeats the final 50 tokens of each chunk at the start of the next.
